title: Mounjaro Meal Plan: 7 Days of Small, Protein-First Meals (2026)
description: A simple 7-day Mounjaro meal plan: protein-first small meals with grams per meal, steady carb portions, a nausea-week version, batch prep and foods to skip.

body_html:
Mounjaro shrinks your appetite fast. A lot of people starting tirzepatide find that a normal dinner plate is now three or four meals' worth of food. And a lot of Mounjaro users are also managing type 2 diabetes, so it isn't only about eating less. It's about eating steady: enough protein to protect muscle, carbs in sensible portions, and no long gaps followed by one big meal.

This 7-day Mounjaro meal plan is built for that. Every meal is small, protein comes first, carbs are portioned and paired with protein, and each day lands at roughly 85 to 100 grams of protein. Your own targets for protein and carbs depend on your size, your blood sugar and your other medications, so set them with your prescriber or a dietitian. Every food here comes from the Mounjaro food list.

The Rules Behind This Mounjaro Meal Plan

Five rules do most of the work. They apply whether you take Mounjaro for diabetes, for weight, or both, and they work the same way on Zepbound (same drug), Ozempic and Wegovy.

  1. Protein first, carbs last. Eat the chicken or eggs before the rice or bread. If you stop early, the protein is already in, and carbs eaten after protein and vegetables tend to hit your blood sugar more gently.
  2. Small, steady carbs. About 1/4 to 1/2 cup of rice, potato, beans or oats per meal, or one slice of whole-grain bread. Roughly the same amount at each meal keeps things predictable.
  3. Four or five eating times. Three small meals plus one or two protein snacks. No skipping until dinner and then trying to eat a full plate.
  4. Stop at the first sign of full. On tirzepatide, the gap between "done" and "too much" can be a single bite.
  5. Sip between meals, not during. Water fills the stomach and leaves less room for protein.

If you take insulin or another diabetes medication that can cause lows, eating much less on Mounjaro can change what you need. Ask your prescriber before you start any new eating plan, including this one.

Batch Prep: 30 Minutes on Sunday

The plan only works if the protein is cooked before you're hungry, because on Mounjaro you may not get hungry at all. On Sunday:

  • Bake 1.5 lb chicken thighs or breast. Slice half, shred half.
  • Brown 1 lb lean ground turkey with onion and taco spice. It covers two dinners and a lunch.
  • Hard-boil 8 eggs.
  • Cook one pot of grains — brown rice or quinoa — and portion it into 1/4-cup scoops so the carb serving is already measured.
  • Roast two sheet pans of vegetables — broccoli, peppers, zucchini, carrots.
  • Stock the no-cook backups: Greek yogurt cups, cottage cheese, string cheese, canned tuna and salmon pouches, ready-to-drink protein shakes.

The 7-Day Mounjaro Meal Plan

Protein grams are approximate and vary by brand. Totals are rounded. Swap anything with the list further down.

Day 1 — about 94 g protein

  • Breakfast: 2 hard-boiled eggs and 1/2 cup cottage cheese — 25 g. Zero cooking, mostly protein.
  • Lunch: 3 oz sliced chicken over roasted vegetables, 1/4 cup brown rice — 28 g. Chicken first, rice last.
  • Snack: 1 string cheese and 10 almonds — 9 g. Two to three hours after lunch.
  • Dinner: 3 oz baked salmon, 1/2 cup green beans, half a small sweet potato — 22 g. Salmon is soft and easy to eat in small bites.
  • Evening: 3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt — 17 g. Add cinnamon instead of honey.

Day 2 — about 90 g protein

  • Breakfast: 1/3 cup oats cooked in milk with half a scoop of protein powder — 22 g. The protein turns oatmeal from a carb meal into a balanced one.
  • Lunch: tuna salad (1 can tuna, Greek yogurt, celery) on 1 slice whole-grain bread — 28 g. Open-faced keeps the bread to one slice.
  • Snack: 2 hard-boiled eggs — 12 g.
  • Dinner: taco bowl — 3 oz seasoned ground turkey, 1/4 cup black beans, lettuce, salsa — 24 g. Skip the chips; beans are the carb.
  • Evening: 1/4 cup cottage cheese — 6 g. Only if you have room.

Day 3 — about 96 g protein

  • Breakfast: ready-to-drink protein shake, sipped over 30 minutes — 30 g. For mornings when solid food sounds like a chore.
  • Lunch: 3 oz deli turkey and 1 oz cheese rolled in a small whole-wheat tortilla — 25 g. Packs in a bag, no reheating.
  • Snack: 1/2 cup shelled edamame — 9 g. Protein and fiber in one.
  • Dinner: 3 oz shredded chicken in 1 cup chicken-vegetable soup — 26 g. Soup is the easiest dinner on low-appetite days.
  • Evening: single-serve Greek yogurt cup — 6 to 15 g depending on brand.

Day 4 — about 88 g protein

  • Breakfast: 2-egg veggie scramble with spinach and peppers, 1/2 slice toast — 14 g. Cook in a light spray, not butter.
  • Lunch: leftover taco turkey (3 oz) over greens with salsa — 22 g. The batch prep paying off.
  • Snack: 3/4 cup plain Greek yogurt with a few berries — 17 g.
  • Dinner: 4 oz shrimp sautéed with zucchini, 1/4 cup quinoa — 25 g. Shrimp cooks in four minutes.
  • Evening: 1 cup milk or unsweetened soy milk — 8 g.

Day 5 — about 92 g protein

  • Breakfast: 3/4 cup cottage cheese with sliced peach — 19 g. Canned peaches in juice work.
  • Lunch: chicken salad (3 oz chicken, Greek yogurt dressing) in lettuce cups, a few whole-grain crackers — 27 g.
  • Snack: 1 oz low-sugar jerky — 10 g. Chew slowly.
  • Dinner: 3 oz pork tenderloin, roasted carrots and broccoli, 1/4 cup brown rice — 24 g. Pork tenderloin is as lean as chicken breast.
  • Evening: half a protein shake — 12 to 15 g. Only if the day came up short.

Day 6 — about 86 g protein

  • Breakfast: 2 eggs and 1/4 cup egg whites, 1 small corn tortilla, salsa — 18 g. A small breakfast taco.
  • Lunch: 1 cup lentil soup with 2 oz shredded chicken stirred in — 25 g. Lentils add fiber without much fat.
  • Snack: 2 string cheese — 14 g.
  • Dinner: 3 oz cod baked with lemon, 1/2 cup roasted vegetables, half a small potato — 20 g. Mild and easy on the stomach.
  • Evening: 1/2 cup cottage cheese — 12 g.

Day 7 — about 98 g protein

  • Breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait — 3/4 cup yogurt, 2 tbsp low-sugar granola, berries — 19 g.
  • Lunch: salmon pouch on 1 slice whole-grain toast with cucumber — 22 g. No cooking.
  • Snack: 2 hard-boiled eggs — 12 g. Last two from the batch.
  • Dinner: chicken stir-fry — 3 oz chicken, peppers, broccoli, 1/4 cup rice — 27 g. Light on the oil and sauce.
  • Evening: ready-to-drink protein shake, half or whole — 15 to 30 g. Then start next week's prep.

The Nausea-Week Version

The days after starting Mounjaro or moving up a dose are when nausea, early fullness and food aversions usually show up. Don't force the regular plan. Switch to this lighter version for a few days and go back once your appetite settles:

  1. Six mini meals — a few bites every two to three hours instead of four or five meals.
  2. Cold, plain protein — Greek yogurt (15 to 17 g), cottage cheese (12 g per 1/2 cup) and protein shakes usually sit better than hot or greasy food.
  3. Broth with shredded chicken — 12 to 15 g. One cup of broth with 2 ounces of chicken.
  4. Crackers with string cheese — 8 to 10 g. Plain, dry and easy.
  5. Soft scrambled egg whites — about 13 g per 1/2 cup.
  6. Small, plain carbs — a few crackers, half a banana, 1/4 cup rice. Keep portions small and pair them with one of the proteins above.

Aim for 60 to 70 grams of protein on the hardest days instead of giving up on it. If you have diabetes, eating very little can affect your blood sugar, so check with your prescriber about what to do on low-intake days. If vomiting or not keeping fluids down lasts more than a day, call them. More ideas are in what to eat when GLP-1 nausea hits.

Swap List: Trade Like for Like

  • Chicken breast (3 oz, ~26 g) ↔ turkey breast, pork tenderloin, shrimp, or 5 oz firm tofu.
  • Salmon (3 oz, ~22 g) ↔ cod, canned salmon, or one can of tuna.
  • Greek yogurt (3/4 cup, ~17 g) ↔ skyr, 3/4 cup cottage cheese, or half a protein shake.
  • 2 eggs (~12 g) ↔ 1/2 cup egg whites, 2 string cheese, or 1 oz jerky.
  • Carb serving (1/4 cup rice or quinoa) ↔ 1/4 cup beans, half a small potato, 1 small corn tortilla, or 1 slice whole-grain bread.

Vegetarian? Lean on tofu, tempeh, eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, edamame and lentils. The GLP-1 protein foods list ranks dozens more by grams per bite.

What to Skip on Mounjaro

  • Fried and greasy food — fries, fried chicken, pizza. Fat slows an already slow stomach even more.
  • Sugary drinks — soda, juice, sweet coffee drinks. Fast sugar, no protein, no fullness.
  • Big bowls of pasta, rice or cereal — a large carb portion with little protein is hard on blood sugar and leaves no room for anything else.
  • Desserts and pastries — save them for an occasional few bites after a protein meal.
  • Carbonated drinks — even diet soda can add pressure and bloating.
  • Alcohol — empty calories, often poorly tolerated on a GLP-1, and it can affect blood sugar. Ask your prescriber what is safe for you.

Why a Printed Meal Plan Isn't Enough

A meal plan assumes you eat what is written. On Mounjaro you won't. You'll finish half of Tuesday's dinner, skip a snack, eat out on Saturday and have no idea whether the day landed at 60 grams of protein or 100, or how much of it was carbs. Those short days add up over a few months.

HealthyOne closes that gap. Snap a photo of the plate or say "half a salmon fillet and some green beans" and it logs what you actually ate. The dashboard puts protein first, GLP-1 mode sets targets built for appetite-suppressing medications, and 50-plus nutrients underneath show the carbs, fiber and micronutrients that slip when meals get small. People ask how it compares to other trackers; we cover that in the nutrient tracker comparison. The point is simple: you see the gap by mid-afternoon, while a yogurt cup can still fix it.

Related Plans and Lists

On a different GLP-1? The Zepbound food list uses the same drug as Mounjaro, and the Wegovy food list covers semaglutide, which is also in Ozempic. The eating rules are nearly identical across all four.

faq.q: What is a good meal plan for Mounjaro?
faq.a: Small, protein-first meals four or five times a day, with modest carb portions paired with protein and plenty of vegetables. Many GLP-1 users aim for roughly 85 to 100 grams of protein a day, but your own target should come from your prescriber or a dietitian.

faq.q: Can I use this Mounjaro meal plan if I have type 2 diabetes?
faq.a: The plan keeps carbs in steady, small portions and pairs them with protein, which suits many people with type 2 diabetes. If you take insulin or another medication that can cause low blood sugar, ask your prescriber before changing how much you eat.

faq.q: What should I eat on Mounjaro when I feel nauseous?
faq.a: Go smaller and plainer for a few days: Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, protein shakes, broth with shredded chicken, egg whites and crackers with string cheese. Skip fried and greasy food. If nausea or vomiting doesn't settle, call your prescriber.

faq.q: Is a Mounjaro meal plan the same as a Zepbound meal plan?
faq.a: Yes, the eating approach is the same. Mounjaro and Zepbound are both tirzepatide, so appetite and fullness work the same way. The plan also fits Ozempic and Wegovy users.

bottom_line: A Mounjaro meal plan works when it is built for the appetite you have now: small meals, protein first, steady carb portions, four or five eating times a day and a lighter version for nausea weeks. Prep the protein and portion the grains on Sunday, swap freely within the list, skip the fried and sugary, and track what you really ate, because on tirzepatide the plan and the plate rarely match.
